16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0d4jeey7vh.xp.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0kzqqn_tds32y.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/01vai7bech1ax.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/148ko75-ihlmp.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0dbjn8dk_o~kd.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0qnkln~4s7ens.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0k2ux72hfk-fi.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T44d,The evaluation uses τ-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench, covering customer-service tool interaction, multi-application API workflows, and office automation. Baselines include SIMIA, an in-context single-shot simulation method, and WM-Training for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. AWM substantially improves over SIMIA across backbones. With DeepSeek-V4-Pro, AWM @16 reaches 86.00 on τ-bench versus SIMIA’s 60.00, 90.70 on AppWorld versus 37.98, and 77.42/69.47/23.21 on OfficeBench 1App/2Apps/3Apps. With GPT-5.4, AWM @16 reports 82.00 on τ-bench, 87.60 on AppWorld, and 63.44 on OfficeBench 1App, compared with SIMIA’s 50.00, 31.01, and 27.96. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, AWM outperforms SIMIA and often matches or exceeds WM-Training; for OfficeBench 3Apps @16, it reports 41.96 versus WM-Training’s 33.04. Removing the Python program tool consistently lowers success rates, with average drops of roughly 5.3–8.1 points for GPT-5.4 and 4.3–7.3 points for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Increasing simulator-side compute from M=1 to M=4 yields gains ranging from about 1.2 to 24.1 points depending on benchmark and backbone.18:T590,The authors instantiate continuous diffusion language modeling with LangFlow and speculative drafting with DSpark. DSpark’s Markov and recurrent-head variants are adapted into standalone generators: they no longer receive target-model features and are not verified or corrected by a target LM. The task is unconditional single-block OpenWebText generation at block lengths 16, 128, and 1024. Because there is no semantic prompt or prior block, each model must choose content and maintain the dependencies induced by that choice. LangFlow repeatedly refines continuous representations for the whole sequence, allowing positions to exchange information before tokens are finalized. The DSpark-style models compute backbone features once and rely on a lightweight output head: the Markov head conditions only on the previous sampled token, while the recurrent head carries a hidden state over the generated history. The analysis identifies a concrete limitation of the Markov interface: information about an earlier choice may no longer be recoverable from the immediately preceding token, restricting the class of distributions the head can represent. Recurrent memory removes that particular access bottleneck, although learning to use the memory remains empirical. The paper also separates improved supervision from improved sampling compute by testing teacher probability matching and additional LangFlow denoising steps.19:T57e,The starting point is a continuous flow language model over categorical sequences. Tokens are represented as one-hot vectors, the source distribution is Gaussian noise, and the model learns a denoiser along a continuous path from noise to data. Existing flow-map language models learn the solution operator X_{s,t}, often parameterized through a two-time denoiser δ_{s,t}, so that generation can jump directly from s=0 to t=1 in one forward pass. In the synchronous version, all token positions share the same scalar time, so every position denoises at the same rate.

Asynchronous FMLMs replace this scalar time with tokenwise times τ_i. Each τ_i measures the denoising progress of position i. A scheduler controls how these tokenwise times evolve. The schedule may be prescribed, or it may be learned and state-adaptive, in the spirit of masked diffusion samplers that decide which positions should be resolved earlier. The technical step that makes this well-defined is to treat the tokenwise times as part of the dynamical state. The model then follows a coupled flow over token representations and their time variables. The paper shows that this coupled process defines a valid flow map and derives distillation objectives for learning it. The resulting one-step model predicts both token evolution and time evolution, internalizing an ordering that would otherwise require multiple sampling steps.1a:T5b5,The experiments cover OLMoE-1B-7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and Moonlight-16B-A3B, all with 64-expert MoE layouts, plus Granite-3.0-3B-A800M for an additional router-normalization test. Pruning ratios include 25%, 50%, and 75%; at 50% pruning the paper also crosses four expert-selection criteria with the main replacement operators. The gate-scale effect is large. On routers trained without top-k renormalization, preserving the trained scale improves OLMoE by about 4.50, 3.39, and 3.09 points at 25%, 50%, and 75% pruning, and improves DeepSeek-V2-Lite by about 0.79, 4.67, and 8.47 points. On routers trained with renormalization, the direction reverses in the relevant settings: Moonlight gains about 1.68 and 1.60 points at 50% and 75%, and Granite gains about 2.08 points at 50%. The tilted novice adds only 1.2%–1.8% parameters at 50% pruning and improves over the constant novice by 3.45 points on OLMoE and 1.37 points on Moonlight, with Holm-corrected significance. At 75% pruning it improves over the constant on all three main models, with corrected significance on two. On OLMoE, a rank-8 tilted novice beats retaining one additional expert per layer while using about one sixth of the parameters; at 75% pruning it reduces WikiText perplexity from 1434 to 172. Under 4-bit and 3-bit GPTQ, the tilted novice’s gain over the constant is not detectably reduced in 11 of 12 settings, while rerouting gains drop in 11 of 12 settings, significantly in 5.1b:T4a9,The authors learn binary gates over attention heads while keeping all model weights frozen. Each head output is multiplied by a hard binary gate in the forward pass; gradients are passed through a sigmoid relaxation with a straight-through estimator. The objective penalizes configurations that exceed a target perplexity ratio while encouraging sparsity. The reported setup initializes all gate logits to 5.0, uses r=1.00, λ=1e-4, AdamW with learning rate 1e-2, batch size 8, and 1,000 optimization steps. The selected pruning mask is the one with the best observed batch-level perplexity ratio during training, not necessarily the final step. Memorization is measured with k-extractability: given the first k tokens, the model is counted as memorizing the sequence if greedy decoding reproduces the next k tokens exactly. The paper evaluates k=16, 32, and 50. For mechanism, it examines attention entropy, softmax saturation, agreement across heads, and the contribution of pruned heads to the residual stream. The key observation is that memorized sequences induce sharper attention and stronger cross-head agreement; pruning task-redundant heads weakens this coordinated retrieval signal.1c:T4a1,The study uses three instruction-tuned models: Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3.5-4B, and Llama-3.1-8B. Qwen3.5 includes many gated-delta linear attention layers. The authors train LoRA adapters for 12 tasks spanning response conventions, behavioral dispositions, and task capabilities: German-only responses, lowercase responses, blanket refusal, chain-of-thought behavior, several misalignment and sycophancy settings, JSON extraction, semantic parsing, and Georgian/Hungarian grapheme-to-phoneme conversion. Each task uses 43–150 evaluation prompts and 20 completions per prompt, so each reported rate aggregates 860–3,000 completions, with 95% confidence intervals bootstrapped over prompts. The main finding is that some fine-tuned behaviors, including German responses and emergent misalignment, can be transferred from the fine-tuned model to the base model through KV-cache patching. Conversely, base→ft patching can partially or fully suppress fine-tuned behavior. Increasing source-cache ownership from prompt-1 to prompt to all generally preserves or strengthens the effect. The model predicts the clean token at the same position, removing the shifted-label convention used in AR training, and applies a 1/t factor to correct for the sampled masking rate. Architecturally, the causal attention mask in every layer is replaced with a bidirectional mask, so prompt, answer, and padding positions can attend to each other. The only trainable parameters are LoRA adapters on self-attention query and value projections, with rank 1024, alpha 1024, and zero dropout. The backbone, embeddings, LM head, biases, and normalization layers remain frozen. Existing single-token strings are reused as mask tokens, avoiding vocabulary expansion. A larger probability drop after scrambling is treated as evidence that the original step order causally supports the answer. 或 JS divergence 对齐教师分布。TESD 修改了这一点：不只让学生生成 rollout，也让自教师生成 rollout，并让教师 rollout 接收环境反馈。奖励由两部分组成：task correctness 衡量解题是否正确，context independence 衡量教师是否只是依赖 privileged context 复述，而不是生成可独立成立的解法。基于这些奖励，TESD 做两类优化。第一是 teacher-oriented optimization，把教师 rollout 的奖励作为训练目标，提升模型在带 privileged context 条件下产生可靠指导的能力。第二是 adaptive student-oriented optimization，把教师奖励作为样本级权重，降低不可靠教师样本对学生蒸馏
